title: Participles as adjectives: thrilling films and second-hand bargains
goal: Use both Swedish participles as adjectives — the present participle in *-ande/-ende* (*en spännande film*) and the past participle with full agreement (*en begagnad cykel, ett begagnat bord, begagnade möbler*).
bekal: you can describe films, books and experiences with present participles: *spännande, rörande, förvirrande*
you can form and agree past participles from all four verb groups, indefinite and definite
you can bargain at a Swedish *loppis* and describe the condition of things
wave: Go back to Svenska 102, Unit 6: read the dialogue again and underline every participle after *bli* and *vara* (*inbjuden*, *stängd* …). For each one, say all three forms aloud — *stängd, stängt, stängda* — then use it in front of a noun: *en stängd dörr, ett stängt fönster*.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Efter filmen
dialogs.intro: A rainy Thursday in November. Dian and Leila have just seen a new Danish thriller at Hagabion, a small cinema in the Linné district. Outside, under the umbrellas, the verdict begins.

lines.speaker: Leila:
lines.text: Nå, vad tyckte du? Visst var den spännande?
lines.id: So, what did you think? It was exciting, wasn't it?
lines.literal: well, what thought you? surely was it exciting?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Jättespännande! Men slutet var lite förvirrande.
lines.id: Super exciting! But the ending was a bit confusing.
lines.literal: giant-exciting! but end-the was little confusing.

lines.speaker: Leila:
lines.text: Ja, och väldigt överraskande. Jag trodde aldrig att det var systern.
lines.id: Yes, and really surprising. I never thought it was the sister.
lines.literal: yes, and very surprising. I believed never that it was sister-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Inte jag heller. Och skådespelerskan som spelade henne — är hon känd?
lines.id: Neither did I. And the actress who played her — is she famous?
lines.literal: not I either. and actress-the who played her — is she known?

lines.speaker: Leila:
lines.text: Ja, hon är en av Danmarks mest uppskattade skådespelare. Hon har vunnit massor av priser.
lines.id: Yes, she's one of Denmark's most highly regarded actors. She's won loads of awards.
lines.literal: yes, she is one of Denmark's most appreciated actors. she has won masses of prizes.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Hon var fantastisk i scenen i den övergivna fabriken.
lines.id: She was fantastic in the scene in the abandoned factory.
lines.literal: she was fantastic in scene-the in the abandoned factory-the.

lines.speaker: Leila:
lines.text: Den var skrämmande. Jag satt med händerna för ögonen.
lines.id: That was terrifying. I sat with my hands over my eyes.
lines.literal: it was frightening. I sat with hands-the before eyes-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Det märkte jag! Men tur att filmen var textad. Jag förstår inte mycket danska utan text.
lines.id: I noticed! But lucky the film had subtitles. I don't understand much Danish without them.
lines.literal: that noticed I! but luck that film-the was texted. I understand not much Danish without text.

lines.speaker: Leila:
lines.text: Det gör inte alla svenskar heller. Ska vi ta en öl på Järntorget?
lines.id: Not all Swedes do either. Shall we have a beer at Järntorget?
lines.literal: that do not all Swedes either. shall we take a beer on Järntorget?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Gärna, men bara en. Imorgon har vi ett avgörande möte med kunden.
lines.id: Sure, but just one. Tomorrow we have a decisive meeting with the client.
lines.literal: gladly, but only one. tomorrow have we a deciding meeting with customer-the.

lines.speaker: Leila:
lines.text: Klokt. Karin säger att din presentation ser lovande ut.
lines.id: Wise. Karin says your presentation looks promising.
lines.literal: wise. Karin says that your presentation looks promising out.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Hoppas det. Jag är fortfarande lite nervös inför den.
lines.id: I hope so. I'm still a bit nervous about it.
lines.literal: hope it. I am still little nervous before it.

notes: **Spännande** (**SPEN-nahn-deh**) — the present participle of *spänna* (to stretch, to tense), so literally "tensing". The ending is **-ande** for most verbs and **-ende** for verbs whose stem ends in a long vowel: *gå* → *gående*, *le* → *leende*, *bo* → *boende*. It never changes for gender or number: *en spännande film, ett spännande år, spännande filmer, den spännande filmen*.

**Förvirrande** / **överraskande** / **skrämmande** — confusing, surprising, frightening: all present participles, all the Swedish equivalents of English adjectives in *-ing*. A whole family of film-review words comes from this one ending: *rörande* (moving), *irriterande* (annoying), *tröttande* (tiring), *underhållande* (entertaining).

**Känd** and **uppskattad** — past participles used as everyday adjectives. *Känd* (**shend**) from *känna* (to know) means "well-known, famous"; *uppskattad* (**ÜP-skaht-tahd**) from *uppskatta* means "appreciated, well-liked".

**Den övergivna fabriken** — *övergiven* (abandoned) is the participle of the strong verb *överge* (to abandon), so it ends in *-en*. In the definite form it becomes *övergivna*: *den övergivna fabriken*, exactly like the plural. Strong participles: *-en* / *-et* / *-na*.

**Filmen var textad** — Swedes subtitle almost everything instead of dubbing it, which is one reason their English is so good. *Textad* (**TEKS-tahd**) = subtitled; *dubbad* = dubbed. Only children's films are dubbed. Danish films are subtitled too — written Danish is easy for Swedes, but spoken Danish is famously hard even for them, which is Leila's point.

**Ett avgörande möte** / **ser lovande ut** — *avgörande* (decisive) is the present participle of the particle verb *avgöra* (to decide), fused just as you saw in Unit 7. *Lovande* (**LOH-vahn-deh**, promising) comes from *lova* (to promise) — word for word the same image as English "promising".

grammars.title: The present participle: -ande / -ende
body: Form it from the infinitive: verbs in *-a* drop the *-a* and add **-ande**; short verbs ending in another vowel add **-ende**. It looks like English *-ing*, and as an adjective it works like *-ing* too. It does **not** agree.
after: Notice the nouns: a present participle can name a **person** who does something (*en sökande* = someone who applies), and the plural is the same word: *alla sökande*. A few become *ett*-nouns for the action itself: *ett leende* (a smile), *ett meddelande* (a message).

**The big warning:** Swedish never uses *-ande* to build a progressive tense. "I am reading" is *jag läser*, never *jag är läsande*. The present participle is an adjective, an adverb or a noun — not a verb form.
As an **adverb** it can strengthen another adjective: *överraskande bra* (surprisingly good), *skrämmande likt* (frighteningly similar), *förbluffande enkelt* (astonishingly simple).

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Loppis i Majorna
dialogs.intro: Saturday morning. Majorna is full of flea markets (*loppisar*) in the autumn, and Dian needs a chest of drawers for her room. Oskar has come along — he claims he knows everything about old furniture.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Titta, en begagnad cykel för fyrahundra kronor. Den ser nästan ny ut.
lines.id: Look, a used bike for four hundred kronor. It looks almost new.
lines.literal: look, a used bicycle for four-hundred crowns. it looks almost new out.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Bromsarna ser slitna ut, och kedjan är rostig.
lines.id: The brakes look worn, and the chain is rusty.
lines.literal: brakes-the look worn out, and chain-the is rusty.

lines.speaker: Säljaren:
lines.text: Den servades i somras, och däcken är nybytta.
lines.id: It was serviced this summer, and the tires are newly replaced.
lines.literal: it serviced-was in summer, and tires-the are new-changed.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Okej. Och den där målade stolen — vad kostar den?
lines.id: OK. And that painted chair — how much is it?
lines.literal: okay. and the there painted chair-the — what costs it?

lines.speaker: Säljaren:
lines.text: Den är tyvärr redan såld. Men byrån bredvid har nedsatt pris: trehundra.
lines.id: That one's already sold, unfortunately. But the chest of drawers next to it is reduced: three hundred.
lines.literal: it is unfortunately already sold. but chest-the beside has down-set price: three-hundred.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Den är ju handgjord! Titta på de snidade blommorna.
lines.id: But it's handmade! Look at the carved flowers.
lines.literal: it is you-know hand-made! look on the carved flowers-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Den är vacker, men en av lådorna är sprucken.
lines.id: It's beautiful, but one of the drawers is cracked.
lines.literal: it is beautiful, but one of drawers-the is cracked.

lines.speaker: Säljaren:
lines.text: Det är därför den är så billig. Med lite lim blir den som ny.
lines.id: That's why it's so cheap. With a bit of glue it'll be good as new.
lines.literal: it is therefore it is so cheap. with little glue becomes it like new.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Jag kan laga den åt dig. Det är inget svårt.
lines.id: I can fix it for you. It's nothing difficult.
lines.literal: I can mend it for you. it is nothing difficult.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Då tar jag byrån. Kan du reservera den åt mig? Vi kommer tillbaka med bil om en timme.
lines.id: Then I'll take the chest of drawers. Can you reserve it for me? We'll be back with a car in an hour.
lines.literal: then take I chest-the. can you reserve it for me? we come back with car in an hour.

lines.speaker: Säljaren:
lines.text: Visst. Jag sätter en lapp på den: ”Reserverad – Dian”.
lines.id: Sure. I'll put a note on it: "Reserved – Dian".
lines.literal: sure. I put a note on it: reserved – Dian.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Och cykeln, då? Nu när däcken är nybytta…
lines.id: And what about the bike? Now that the tires are new…
lines.literal: and bicycle-the, then? now when tires-the are new-changed…

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: En sak i taget. Mitt rum är redan fullt av begagnade saker!
lines.id: One thing at a time. My room is already full of second-hand things!
lines.literal: one thing in time-the. my room is already full of used things!

notes: **En begagnad cykel** — *begagnad* (**beh-GAHNG-nahd**, used, second-hand) is a past participle that has become an ordinary adjective. Group 1 verbs give *-ad / -at / -ade*: *en begagnad cykel, ett begagnat bord, begagnade saker*. The *gn* is said **ngn**, as in *regn*.

**Bromsarna ser slitna ut** — *sliten* (**SLEE-ten**, worn) comes from the strong verb *slita* (*slet, slitit*), so it follows the strong pattern *sliten / slitet / slitna*. *Se … ut* (to look, to appear) is a particle verb: the adjective goes between the two parts.

**Däcken är nybytta** — Swedish loves gluing *ny-* (newly) onto a participle: *nybakad* (freshly baked), *nymålad* (freshly painted), *nyfödd* (newborn), *nyutexaminerad* (newly graduated). The participle *bytt* (from *byta*) agrees with the plural *däcken*: *nybytta*.

**Den där målade stolen** — in the definite form, every participle takes its plural-looking ending: *den målade stolen, det målade bordet, de målade stolarna*. For group 1 verbs that ending is *-ade*, which looks exactly like the past tense — context tells you which is which. *Såld* (sold) is irregular, like the verb *sälja – sålde*: *såld / sålt / sålda*.

**Handgjord** / **sprucken** — *gjord* (**yood**) is the participle of *göra*: *gjord / gjort / gjorda*, so *handgjord* = handmade. *Sprucken* (cracked) comes from *spricka* (*sprack, spruckit*), one of the *i-a-u* strong verbs from Unit 2 — and its participle has the same *u* as the supine.

**Loppis** (**LOP-pis**), short for *loppmarknad*, is a national hobby. In Göteborg's Majorna, people set up tables in courtyards and on the pavement on autumn weekends, and charity shops such as Myrorna and Erikshjälpen sell second-hand everything. Bargaining is allowed, but gently: *Går du ner lite på priset?*

grammars.title: The past participle: one recipe per verb group
body: As an adjective, the past participle agrees exactly like *stor / stort / stora*: one form for *en*-words, one for *ett*-words, and one for plurals and definite forms. The shape depends on the verb group.
after: Indefinite: *en målad stol, ett skrivet brev, sydda kläder*. Definite: *den målade stolen, det skrivna brevet, de sydda kläderna* — with double definiteness, as with any adjective.
Group 2a verbs whose stem ends in *-d* or *-nd* keep it simple: *använda* → *använd / använt / använda*; *tända* → *tänd / tänt / tända*.
For strong verbs, start from the supine and swap *-it* for *-en*: *skrivit* → *skriven*, *bjudit* → *bjuden*, *brutit* → *bruten*, *stulit* → *stulen*.

sections.title: Participles everywhere: signs, ads and reviews

blocks.text: Once you know the two participles, you will see them on every street. Signs, ads and reviews love them because they pack a whole clause into one word: *en film som spänner en* becomes *en spännande film*; *en cykel som någon har använt* becomes *en begagnad cykel*.

Meaning
rows: Pedestrians, please use the other side

blocks.text: In reviews, present participles carry the verdict: *en **rörande** berättelse* (a moving story), *ett **underhållande** program* (an entertaining show), *en **tröttande** roman* (a tiring novel). Pair them with the adverbs you know — *otroligt, väldigt, lite* — and you can review anything.

blocks.title: -ande or -ad? Feeling vs cause
items: English *bored/boring*, *confused/confusing* have Swedish twins: the **present** participle describes what **causes** the feeling, the **past** participle describes the person who **feels** it.
*Föreläsningen var tröttande.* — *Studenterna var trötta.* (Here Swedish uses the plain adjective.)

blocks.text: Condition words are the vocabulary of every second-hand ad on *Blocket*, Sweden's big classifieds site: *i nyskick* (as new), *välvårdad* (well kept), *sliten men hel* (worn but intact), *lätt använd* (lightly used), *säljes p.g.a. flytt* (for sale because of a move). Notice how many of them are participles.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Unit 2
items: Take one verb from each strong-verb family in Unit 2 and add the participle: *skriva → skriven*, *dricka → drucken*, *bjuda → bjuden*, *bära → buren*.
Then put each one in front of a noun in all three forms: *ett skrivet brev, en skriven text, skrivna regler*.
Finally use the definite form: *det skrivna brevet*.
